properties.name: A scoped answer actually narrows, so "my part" is a different answer from "the program"
properties.statement:
Scoping a detector to a part of the design must return an answer materially different from the unscoped one, or the narrowing is decoration and the number beside it is misleading.

(Distinct from the FACT, which records the measurement, and from the DECISION, which proposes one specific default. This is the intent both of those serve: the fact is evidence, the decision is one answer, and this says what must be true whatever answer is chosen.)

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES THIS A REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. Driving the built binary over all 56 Components of reflow2's own design (2487 nodes, 83 gaps), at the DEFAULT depth of 3: every single component returns 50-60 of the 83 gaps, median 55, over a region of 595-903 nodes. The spread across all 56 is 50..60 — indistinguishable. `in_scope: 55, out_of_scope: 28` reads as "your part has 55 gaps" and says the same thing to every team about every part. Shallower depths discriminate sharply: depth 1 gives 0-19 gaps over 17-139 nodes, depth 2 gives 2-27 over 267-601. Evidence: `fact:defect-a-scoped-detector-at-its-default-depth-returns-two-thirds-of-the-design`.

WHAT IS OWED. Not a number — a property. A scoped read should be checkable against the claim it makes: if scoping to any seed returns most of what the unscoped call returns, the tool should be able to SAY SO rather than leaving the reader to compare two numbers they were never shown together. The specific default is `dec:the-default-scope-depth-should-be-two`, which is separately open and is the owner's to settle.

THREE THINGS THE SAME MEASUREMENT TURNED UP, worth carrying together because they are one confusion about what a region is:
(a) `scope.rs` justifies the default of 3 by saying the third hop is needed to reach a contained child component's capabilities. `scope_region` puts the whole containment closure into the seed set BEFORE taking the radius, so those capabilities are ONE hop from an owned node. The stated reason is not a reason the code needs.
(b) `detect_gaps`' description claims its region is "the same computation claim_region uses for 'the part I hold', so 'my area' means one thing everywhere". It is not: the MCP defaults differ (3 vs 2) AND `scope_region` adds the containment closure that `claimed_region` omits.
(c) That second divergence is already recorded in `scope.rs` as possibly a defect in the claims layer, deliberately left unfixed because changing what a claim covers changes what two people believe they hold. Reconciling the two is a bigger question than a default and is NOT assumed here.

SCOPE OF THIS REQUIREMENT, so the increment can be argued with: it is about the scoped DETECTORS and the words they use about themselves. It does not decide (c), and it does not touch `design_regions`, which already reports its own depth and coverage.
